column1: # Brand-name test for the synthetic fixtures in this folder (see README.md).
# Each expected site matches the query at least as well as any look-alike
# and has far stronger popularity signals, so any sensible ranker that blends
# name matching with popularity should get them all. Some names are only
# findable through link text or aliases (bofa, amex, nyt, citibank), and some
# real sites share a name (chase / chase center, delta / delta faucet,
# ford / ford foundation, amazon / amazon jobs). The queries at the end are
# harder: a brand plus what the user wants to do there.
# Brand plus intent: the official site, not the look-alike built for the
# query. A look-alike's title (and for some, link text from one spam page)
# holds every query word, so it matches the text better than the official
# site does, but it has no rank.
# Look-alike domains that spell out the whole query.
# A longer name beats the brand it starts with.
# Little-known sites: github.com has no rank or Wikidata entry here (it is
# only a link target), and no ranked site has its name.
